title: Ciscomani receives District Excellence Award for work in Arizona's 6th Congressional District
text:
Ciscomani receives District Excellence Award for work in Arizona’s 6th Congressional District
Representative Juan Ciscomani was honored with the District Excellence Award by the Institute of Legislative Analysis, recognizing his record of results and federal investments across Arizona’s 6th Congressional District, according to a Sep. 2 announcement.
“My top priority in Congress has always been clear: listening to my constituents,” said Congressman Juan Ciscomani. “I have the privilege of representing an amazing district– it includes ranches, farms, mines, major manufacturing plants, military installations, a national park, part of Arizona’s second largest city and some of the best small towns in Arizona. Delivering real results for the hardworking men and women I work for is my North Star. It’s what drives me. Receiving the District Excellence Award from the Institute of Legislative Analysis is an acknowledgement of that commitment. I am truly grateful for this honor.”
Ryan McGowan, CEO of the Institute for Legislative Analysis, said, “The Institute for Legislative Analysis is proud to present Congressman Juan Ciscomani with the District Excellence Award for earning an 'A+' Grade under ILA’s District-Based Grading system. The Limited Government Index is the first-of-its-kind system that evaluates each Member of Congress based not only on their votes, but also on the unique makeup of their districts. Congressman Ciscomani’s record shows he has stayed committed to advancing the limited government principles of the U.S. Constitution despite representing a competitive district where many lawmakers would cave to big government pressure. We especially appreciate his work to strengthen border security, protect taxpayers, and stand up for families and small businesses across Southern Arizona. Congressman Ciscomani and his team deserve credit for showing that limited government principles are not abstract talking points, but practical solutions tied directly to accountability, affordability, and a government that works for the people it serves.”
Ciscomani secured $42.7 million in funding supporting 20 federal projects across all five counties within his district: Cochise, Graham, Greenlee, Pima, and Pinal. These investments support local priorities such as public safety infrastructure improvements and workforce development initiatives.
The award also highlights Ciscomani's bipartisan leadership; he has ranked among Congress's most bipartisan members two years in a row while serving on both House Appropriations and Veterans’ Affairs Committees—championing national security issues as well as veterans' interests within Arizona.
Local leaders praised Ciscomani's efforts throughout their communities: "Congressman Ciscomani leads by listening,” said Sahuarita Mayor Tom Murphy; Marana Mayor Jon Post added, "He delivers! The congressman has brought critical federal resources back to our community..." Eloy Mayor Andy Sutton said, "Our congressman works across party lines...and brings people together to deliver meaningful results."
Juan Ciscomani is currently serving in U.S. Congress representing Arizona’s 6th district since 2023 after replacing Ann Kirkpatrick; he defeated Kirsten Engel in both 2022 (50.7%–49.2%) and 2024 (50%–47.5%) general elections, according to official congressional records. Born in Hermosillo in 1982 before moving to Tucson where he now lives at age forty; he graduated from University of Arizona with a BA degree.
